$comment: Measured constants for the greenhouse simulator. Every value carries its
provenance: where it came from and when. A number without provenance is
folklore, and folklore in a simulator is worse than no simulator - it
produces confident wrong answers that look like evidence.
burn-2026-09-10   elantris, four burner cycles observed 17:21-18:31 local
the last season the burner ran the same scenario
paired-2026-09-10 one 2-second-apart sample from both sensors
fit-2026-09-11     refit from fit/fit_envelope.py and fit/fit_burner.py
burn-2026-09-12     the first burn with a trustworthy sensor AND known relay state

outdoor_co2_ppm.note: winter baseline settles ~465 raw; 420 outdoor after sensor bias

leak_fraction_per_minute.note: Raised from 0.027. Duty cycle is sink/gross and nothing else - the transport lag stretches a cycle but cannot change its ratio - so 44% measured against 88 ppm/min gross requires ~37 ppm/min of removal at the setpoint. Slightly above the 22-32 ppm/min measured directly after a peak; see known_gaps.

thermal_coupling_per_minute.note: relaxation toward outdoor; provisional, refit from the export

co2_ppm_per_minute.note: Least-squares against elantris's own labelled trace, and consistent with the one long burn: 387->1454 ppm in 14.8 min is +72 ppm/min net, plus ~14 ppm/min of sink at that level.

deg_c_per_minute.note: ~1 C per 15 min of run time

transport_lag_minutes.note: Was 2.5, and that was the single biggest error. Near the setpoint a 7-minute burn nets only +4..+16 ppm/min because most of the output is still in transit when the burner is commanded off - it then arrives as the overshoot, which peaks 2-3 min AFTER the command. 4.5 min reproduces the on-duration exactly (7.2 sim vs 7.0 measured).

clear_fraction_per_minute.note: NOT measured - the fan has never run under tempestas

hps_deg_c_per_minute.note: two HPS fixtures; NOT measured, refit from history-2025 light hours

sites.$comment: CO2 is a real mixing gradient, expressed as a FRACTION of the enrichment above outdoor so it vanishes when nothing is running. Temperature is mostly instrument - the canopy sensor has never had an offset set.

co2_gradient_fraction.note: half the 143 ppm gap over 690 ppm of enrichment; the generator injects here

temp_offset_c.note: elantris is the calibrated sensor, so it defines the reference

co2_gradient_fraction.note: the other half of the gap

temp_offset_c.note: INSTRUMENT bias, not climate - vapour pressure agrees to 2.5%. Set to 0 once calibrated.

known_gaps.$comment: Where the model is knowingly wrong. Recorded so nobody mistakes a fitted number for a measured one, or trusts the simulator past what it has earned.
known_gaps.duty_cycle: Two clean cycles on 2026-09-12: 7.8 min on, 7.3 min off, ~52% duty, against 37% simulated and 44% measured on 2026-09-10. The configured 1400/1500 band is not what the greenhouse actually oscillates over either - dead time on ignition and overshoot on cut-out widen it to roughly 1320-1577. Decay measured cleanly during the off periods (no burner term to disentangle): 30 ppm/min at 1470-1543, 22-26 ppm/min at 1327-1393.
known_gaps.fan_and_lights: Every fan and lights constant is an ESTIMATE. Neither has ever run under tempestas, so nothing has been measured. Do not tune a ventilation or lighting rule against this model until it has.
known_gaps.thermal: thermal_coupling_per_minute is provisional. history-2025 temperatures carry the canopy sensor's uncalibrated offset, so fit time constants and rates from it - never absolute values.
known_gaps.outdoor: The diurnal curve is a sine, not real weather. Use replay mode when the question depends on actual outdoor conditions.
known_gaps.humidity: Transpiration is a flat +0.02 hPa/min with no plant, light or temperature dependence, and vapour is clamped at saturation. Overnight the model therefore parks at 100% RH rather than condensing out. Fine for exercising control paths; not a basis for any humidity rule.
known_gaps.identifiability: Gross output, transport lag and sink cannot be identified simultaneously from 70 minutes of data whose relay transitions are only known to +-30 s - the grid search moved G between 88 and 118 depending on how the trajectory was anchored. The fix is logged relay transitions alongside readings, which tempestas can now produce and the legacy system never did.
known_gaps.sink_shape: The 2025 season (16,744 decay points) cannot distinguish a proportional sink from a constant one - residuals differ by 0.5%. Decay there averages 18.4 ppm/min with a p10-p90 of 3.5-37.7, so the shape is assumed, not measured. Note that spread is real physics: vents, wind, light and crop stage, not noise.
known_gaps.lag_is_asymmetric: THE structural error, measured 2026-09-12. Ignition to first effect was 3.7 min (observed three times); cut-out to overshoot peak was 1.6 min. One symmetric transport lag cannot produce both, which is why no value of it ever satisfied the on-duration and the overshoot together. Physically obvious once seen: lighting a burner takes time that extinguishing it does not - the flame stops instantly and only CO2 already in transit keeps arriving. The model wants an ignition DEAD TIME (~2.5-3 min, nothing happens) separate from a mixing lag (~1.5-2 min, first-order). Do not refit the single tau again; change the shape first.
